newsitem.title: USA: Venezuelan urges multinational force for border.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan urges multinational force for border.

text.p: A Venezuelan senator on Tuesday called for an international peacekeeping force to be deployed on the Venezuelan-Colombian frontier, saying cross-border raids by Colombian armed groups threatened to provoke a wider conflict.

"Relations between Venezuela and Colombia have been seriously disturbed by the violent aggression of armed groups that operate with impunity on the Colombian side of the frontier with Venezuela," Lewis Perez, who is president of the Senate's Defence Committee, said in a statement.
The Colombian government was incapable of stopping the violence and local officials in some areas were supporting the attackers, he said.
Perez made his appeal at a conference of U.S. and Latin American military and defence officials on security strategy for the Americas.

"Given the delicate situation of tension and violence, initiatives such as a multinational peace force could in the short term, and given the urgency of the case, safeguard lives in the region and impede drug traffickers and guerrillas from acting and expanding their actions," he said.
The force would act in frontier zone under the command of the Colombian government.

Armed groups crossed the border daily, kidnapping for ransom and demanding protection money from businesses, Perez said. A number of Venezuelan soldiers and civilians had been killed. Some people in Venezuela were calling for firm action in response, he said.
